business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) Ocean Box Brokerage

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Quebec private law is civil law within the Canadian federal state; public/commercial regulatory law is common law at the federal level)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada 2018
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union, applied provisionally 2017
Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA), in force 2014
Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended, incl. Article 8 on international shipping and air transport income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal — Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.31 et seq. (money laundering and proceeds of crime); United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c. U-2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c. 21; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c. 17. Province of Quebec — Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, as amended by Bill 24 (2023) creating the Quebec beneficial ownership declaration regime for legal persons and partnerships; regulations promulgated under CQLR c. P-44.1; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236–2247 (societe en commandite / limited partnership formation, partner liability and publicity); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, ss. 32 and 32.1 (French business-name rule and trademark exception).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Existence of the foreign corporate general partner (commandite), evidencing valid incorporation and good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the country of origin (e.g., Corporations Canada, a U.S. Secretary of State, or the equivalent foreign registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority in the country of origin (Canada has applied the Hague Apostille Convention since 11 January 2024, so consular legalization is no longer required for Convention states; for non-Convention states, consular legalization through a Quebec or Canadian diplomatic mission applies)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized executed partnership agreement (contrat de societe en commandite) and partners' declaration where executed outside Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of execution, or consular legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of valid government-issued photo identification and proof of residential address for each individual limited partner and each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the partner's or beneficial owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney / mandate appointing the Quebec-registered agent or attorney-in-fact to file the declaration of registration and receive service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the place of signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence screening of every general partner, limited partner and ultimate beneficial owner against: (i) domestic reporting and record-keeping triggers under the PCMLTFA and SOR/2002-184, including suspicious transaction reporting; (ii) the U.S. OFAC SDN List and active U.S. sanctions programs, mandatory because of the SWIFT wire and ACH direct payment rails; (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List and Canadian listings under the United Nations Act, the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky); (iv) domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) and Heads of State lists; and (v) adverse media, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth checks. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by any non-resident PEP, high-risk jurisdiction nexus, opacity in partner funding, or any matched sanction alert, consistent with the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier assigned to this NVOCC freight-forwarding scope.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — Registraire des entreprises du Quebec online services portal: services.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under s. 32 of the Charter of the French Language (CQLR, c. C-11), the name of a Quebec partnership must be in French; a version in another language may be registered only if the French version is declared or the name is a registered trademark under s. 32.1. The REQ applies strict transliteration and grammatical rules requiring French spelling and syntax to be respected, with generic terms normalized into French. The legal element of a Quebec limited partnership must be 'societe en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' in the French name, and 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' in the English version. Names lacking distinctiveness or creating confusion with existing registrations or trademarks will be refused.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens implying banking or financial institution activity: 'Bank', 'Banque', 'Trust', 'Fiducie', 'Finance' — prior OSFI or AMF authorization required
Tokens implying insurance business: 'Insurance', 'Assurance', 'Assurance-vie' — prior AMF (Autorite des marches financiers) licence or authorization required
Tokens implying a university, college or educational institution: 'University', 'Universite', 'College', 'Institut' — prior ministerial authorization required
Tokens implying regulated professions: 'Lawyer', 'Avocat', 'Notary', 'Notaire', 'Engineer', 'Ingenieur', 'Physician', 'Medecin' — prior consent of the relevant professional order required

Tokens implying public, royal or governmental authority: 'Royal', 'Government', 'Gouvernement', 'Municipal', 'Police', 'Commission', 'Ministere' — prior authorization of the competent minister or body required
Tokens implying pharmacy or medical facility: 'Pharmacie', 'Clinique', 'Hospital' — statutory ownership and licensing restrictions apply
Tokens implying charitable or religious status: 'Foundation', 'Fondation', 'Charity', 'Eglise' — supporting documents and licence requirements apply
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The REQ name reservation is valid for 90 days; if the declaration of registration is not filed within that window, the reservation lapses automatically and a new reservation request with a new fee must be submitted. Upon refusal of a requested name, the applicant must first obtain the REQ's written reasons, then may file a request for re-examination / rectification with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal, attaching legal, trademark and linguistic arguments. If the Registraire maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Court of Quebec for judicial review of the Registrar's decision, generally within 30 days of the review decision, in accordance with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR, c. P-44.1) and the Code of Civil Procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible in principle for REQ registration purposes: Quebec law requires a real physical address in Quebec, not a post-office box, at which documents and notices may be served and records examined; a licensed virtual-office or registered-office service with a staffed physical reception room in Quebec will satisfy the bare statutory address requirement. However, for an NVOCC ocean freight forwarding operation classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced and settling via SWIFT wire and ACH direct payment rails, Canadian banks, FINTRAC and commercial counterparties will in practice require demonstrable commercial substance, including staffed premises, operating records and accessible books located in Quebec. A pure virtual office is therefore not recommended as the sole establishment; a serviced office with physical staff and mail and records handling is the market-standard minimum.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 25–30% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of commercial activity. This quantified estimate reflects the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier, the use of SWIFT wire and ACH direct rails, the allowance for non-resident ownership, and the NVOCC sector's exposure to trade-based money laundering and invoice-redirection typologies. FINTRAC does not routinely conduct unannounced premises visits for non-reporting entities, but chartered banks commonly conduct compliance site visits as part of enhanced due diligence before or shortly after account activation, and U.S.-facing NVOCC operations may be examined by the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission in respect of OTI licensing requirements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation of one French corporate name for a societe en commandite with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the regulations promulgated under CQLR, c. P-44.1 (CAD 36 approximately USD 27)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the declaration of registration (declaration d'immatriculation) creating the Quebec societe en commandite / limited partnership
Notarial services for authentication of partners' signatures, notarized copies of non-Quebec identity documents and optional notarized execution of the partnership agreement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary in private practice, Chambre des notaires du Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff and market benchmark (CAD 500–600 per file)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, Book V, Title VII, articles 2230–2240 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, articles 8, 14, 18, and 37.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Business Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a Quebec limited partnership; capital contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement and must be disclosed in the declaration. No escrow account is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the partners hereby adopt the limited partnership agreement as the constitutive document of the partnership and approve the subscription of partnership units in the amounts set forth in Schedule A; FURTHER RESOLVED: that the registered office of the partnership shall be established at [insert address in Quebec] and that the general partner is authorized to execute all documents and pay all fees required for registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; FURTHER RESOLVED: that [name] is appointed as manager to open bank accounts, execute ocean freight forwarding contracts, and maintain all regulatory approvals. The resolutions are effective immediately upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Partnership Agreement Execution and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Quebec Business Registry – online name search and reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute a limited partnership agreement among the general partner and limited partners. Conduct an availability search in the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online enterprise search system and reserve the proposed name electronically. The name must contain a distinctive element and a legal designation indicating limited partnership.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of general partner's identification (e.g., incorporation certificate if corporate general partner)
Proposed partnership name and address of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is reserved by an earlier entity, submit one additional alternative name within 15 days; REQ will process the alternative without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Déclaration d'immatriculation using the REQ 'Déclaration d'immatriculation' electronic form. Provide full legal name of the partnership, registered office address in Quebec, mailing address, names and addresses of all general partners and limited partners, and a detailed description of the business purpose covering NVOCC ocean freight forwarding and brokerage. Pay the statutory filing fee online through the REQ secure payment platform.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney or representational mandate if file is submitted by an agent
Proof of payment of filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of incomplete filing, respond within 30 days through the online follow-up module. If rejection is issued, correct the identified deficiencies and resubmit the declaration within 15 days; no re-notarization is required if the substance remains unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Registration Excerpt and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After REQ approval, obtain the official registration excerpt (immatriculation notice). Use the registration number and excerpt to register with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) account, and with the Canada Revenue Agency for GST/HST and a partnership business number. If payroll is anticipated, apply for payroll account simultaneously. Complete the registration online via the 'CléQC' business services portal or by paper if not eligible.
required_dossiers: Social insurance numbers or business numbers of general partners
Business contact details and estimated revenue thresholds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, contact Revenu Québec's 'Démarrez une entreprise' helpline for expedited processing. If Revenu Québec requests the identity of the representative or a missing declaration (e.g., undertaking form), submit the requested document within 10 business days to avoid a suspension of the QST number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal borough business licensing office and Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence (permis d'exercice d'une entreprise) covering the freight-forwarding office and any ancillary storage. If the partnership operates its own delivery vehicles for pick-up or delivery, obtain the appropriate transport operator authorization from the Société de l'assurance automobile du Québec (SAAQ) and the Ministère des Transports du Québec. Submit the REQ excerpt, occupancy permit, and proof of third-party liability insurance.
required_dossiers: Copy of lease or ownership title for the place of business
Certificate of insurance (general liability and property)
Municipal fire safety inspection certificate for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit is refused, appeal to the municipal council within 30 days on grounds of compliance with zoning and safety by-laws. For transport authorizations, filing a corrective application with SAAQ within 15 days of refusal resolves most documentation deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defense and Occupational Health Safety Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal fire department (Service de sécurité incendie) and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a fire safety certificate confirming compliance with fire prevention regulations for the registered office and any warehousing areas. If the partnership employs workers, register with CNESST and obtain a workplace health and safety clearance. For racked storage areas, submit structural load calculations and stack configuration drawings to the municipal building inspector for approval.
required_dossiers: Fire safety inspection report and evacuation plan
Structural load certificate for any warehouse storage racks
CNESST registration confirmation and first-aid equipment checklist
Workplace communication plan for emergency response
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection identifies violations, undertake corrective measures within 14 days and request a re-inspection. If structural load calculations are rejected, submit revised engineering drawings within 14 days; CNESST refusals may be cured by a formal administrative reconsideration filed within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) – Trade Administration and Licensing Branch
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Broker Licence (under the Customs Act, R.S.C., 1985, c. 1 (2nd Supp.), s. 9)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full provincial EIA for pure office and light-transshipment operations; requires authorization only if the site handles hazardous goods or emits effluent beyond sanitary limits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge without a provincial certificate of authorization; sanitary sewage must comply with municipal sewer by-laws. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from office and container transloading activities must remain below the 5-tonne annual threshold set out in the Clean Air Regulation (Q-2, r.32, Schedule O), with records retained for at least 3 years. Solid waste and empty containers must be transported by carriers holding a valid MELCCFP waste permit, and hazardous waste manifests must be filed when applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire department for the premises; structural integrity inspection for any storage racks; CNESST occupational health and safety clearance (including first aid and emergency escape plans) for offices and freight-handling stations; temporary workplace excavation or loading-dock access permits where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – federal GST/HST and income tax administration, portal: www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency; Revenu Québec (RQ) – Quebec Sales Tax (QST), provincial income tax and payroll, portal: www.revenuquebec.ca; Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and extra-provincial limited partnership registration, portal: www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident limited partnership (LP) carrying on ocean freight forwarding/NVOCC business in Quebec: (1) Determine whether the LP has an establishment in Canada/Quebec, because an extra-provincial LP with a Quebec establishment must register with the REQ and obtain a NEQ. (2) Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) through CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO) by completing RC1W or RC1; the BN serves as the backbone for program accounts: GST/HST (RT), import/export (RM), payroll (RP), and corporate income tax (RC) as applicable. (3) Register separately with Revenu Québec via its 'Mon dossier entreprise' service to obtain a QST number and any QPIP/QHSF payroll accounts. (4) Because a limited partnership is fiscally transparent for federal and Quebec income tax purposes, the tax identification authority should also file the partnership information call (T5013/CO-17) and issue Statements of Partnership Income to each partner. Non-resident partners should appoint a Canadian representative (Form RC59) for CRA service and a mandatary for RQ, where required. Registration is mandatory when taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD $30,000, but non-residents may also elect voluntary GST/HST and QST registration to recover input tax refunds on imported goods and services used in commercial activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a US-style check-the-box election. A Quebec limited partnership is statutorily pass-through for income tax (both federal and Quebec) provided it is not a corporation, trust, or listed entity. Relevant elections include: (i) partnership fiscal-period election under subsection 249.1(5) of the Income Tax Act and equivalent Quebec provision, allowing a non-calendar tax year; (ii) section 97(2) rollover election on property contributed to the partnership by a partner; (iii) GST/HST election under section 247 of the Excise Tax Act to register on a retroactive date or to treat an earlier supply as made in the ordinary course of business; (iv) QST equivalent election instruments under the Quebec Act respecting the Québec sales tax; and (v) for hybrid mismatch purposes, Canada's anti-hybrid rules (sections 18.15, 18.16, and 212.3 et seq.) apply to disallow deductions or reverse withholding exceptions, and no elective waiver is available, so the LP must document each partner's tax classification in its home jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) + QST (Quebec value-added tax) – dual VAT-like consumption tax on supplies in the Province of Quebec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 annual taxable supplies (small-supplier threshold; applies to both federal GST/HST and Quebec QST). For non-resident vendors of cross-border digital services, a special registration threshold of CAD $30,000 in gross revenue applies, with simplified non-resident registration available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or government e-invoice stamping regime. CRA and Revenu Québec accept traditional paper and electronic invoices. Electronic invoices must contain the standard GST/HST/QST disclosure (vendor's BN/QST number, date of supply, consideration, tax charged) and must be retained in an accessible, legible format for six years. GST/HST returns must be filed through CRA's NETFILE/GST Express service; QST returns through Revenu Québec's online filing system. There is no mandatory API interconnection or pre-clearance of invoices, but the CRA operates an e-invoice interoperability pilot using PEPPOL standards for voluntary business-to-government e-procurement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating eligibility for GST/HST and QST on an NVOCC/outbound ocean freight-forwarding operation includes: (a) supply of goods exported by the supplier, delivered by the supplier to a common carrier for export, or delivered to a consignee located outside Canada (Excise Tax Act s. 22 and Schedule VI Part I); (b) supply of a service provided to a non-resident person where the service is not provided in connection with real property in Canada, is not provided to an individual present in Canada, and is not in respect of tangible personal property located in Canada (ETA s. 25, Schedule VI Part V); and (c) supplies of services of arranging for or providing international freight transportation of goods to or from Canada, including ocean containerized cargo under NVOCC bills of lading, which are zero-rated under Schedule VI Parts V and IX. The zero-rating also applies to QST through Quebec's parallel provisions, provided the service is supplied in connection with goods moving outside Canada. The supplier must maintain contemporaneous evidence establishing that the goods were actually exported and that the service was supplied to a non-resident client.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (via CBSA eManifest or Canadian Export Reporting System), including Container Number / SPN
Ocean Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill (master and house if NVOCC) showing Quebec/Canadian port of loading and foreign port of discharge
Commercial invoice and the freight forwarding service contract / NVOCC booking confirmation
Banker's inward remittance evidence (MT103/telegraphic transfer receipt) or SWIFT advice showing receipt of export consideration from the non-resident
CBSA export manifest / prior notice number and, if applicable, proof of marine cargo insurer's risk report
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If an exporter claims zero-rating without full export documentation, CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess the supplies at 5% GST and 9.975% QST (combined 14.975%), deny corresponding input tax credits, and charge arrears interest on the net tax. Additional penalties include: (a) GST/HST gross negligence penalty under s. 285 of the Excise Tax Act, generally 25–50% of the net tax understated; (b) Quebec administrative penalty under the QST Act mirroring the federal regime; (c) Income Tax Act s. 163(2) gross negligence penalty of 50% of misreported income on related partner allocations; (d) monetary penalties under the Customs Act for false declarations in export accounting (up to CAD $25,000 per contravention); and (e) if the misrepresentation is wilful, criminal prosecution for tax evasion under s. 239 of the Income Tax Act and s. 327 of the Excise Tax Act, potentially leading to imprisonment, fines, and disgorgement of refunds. The 180-day repatriation benchmark is retained as an administrative due-diligence indicator: where export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, the CRA may treat the foreign receivable as never created and withdraw zero-rating, irrespective of the absence of a formal Fx-repatriation statute, and the partnership must therefore document the payment within that window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the prudential regulator licensing and supervising Schedule I and II banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/ATF and cross-border electronic funds transfer reporting regulator; for Quebec, the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) registers money services businesses and financial entities operating in the province.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full de jure and de facto convertibility for both current and capital account items, with no exchange controls administered by the Bank of Canada or the Quebec government. Capital injections, operational transfers, profit distributions, and partner capital withdrawals are freely remittable in CAD or any convertible foreign currency without prior government approval. Profit remittance hurdles are tax-driven rather than FX-driven: (i) distributions by the Quebec société en commandite (Limited Partnership) to non-resident limited partners may be subject to Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII and to Part XII.2 tax on partnership distributions to non-resident members unless treaty relief is established; (ii) the partnership must file T5013 information returns and the non-resident partner must obtain treaty clearance (e.g., CRA Form NR301 or equivalent competent authority certificate) before reliance on exemption; (iii) applicable UN/OSFI sanctions screening may delay or block specific wire destinations, but no general repatriation moratorium exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes NO export proceeds surrender obligation, NO mandatory conversion ratio, and NO statutory timeline for converting NVOCC ocean freight or freight-forwarding export receipts. Export earnings may be retained in CAD, USD, or any other convertible currency in domestic or foreign accounts at the commercial discretion of the partnership. The only compliance duties are record-keeping and reporting: (i) every incoming/outgoing electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more must be documented under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC's EFT reporting rules; (ii) shipping and cargo documents (Bills of Lading, house bills, export declarations, cargo manifests) must substantiate the commercial basis of each receipt; (iii) U.S.-related export cargo movements may trigger U.S. Census AES filing requirements, which are operational, not currency-control, obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational USD Clearing Account
Operational CAD Account / FX Forward Hedging Line
Operational Account / U.S. Dollar Correspondent Clearing (BMO Harris)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM-LOW for primary treasury concentration. Canada does not recognize the European Electronic Money Institution (EMI) passport, and a UK FCA-authorised or EU-licensed EMI cannot operate as a bank in Canada. A fintech cross-border provider (e.g., Wise Business, Stripe Treasury, or a FINTRAC-registered Money Services Business) may be engaged only as a supplementary disbursement corridor, provided the provider is registered as an MSB under the PCMLTFA and, if carrying on business in Quebec, holds any applicable AMF licence. The Quebec LP must maintain its primary operating, escrow, and clearing accounts with a Canadian Schedule I bank, because offshore EMIs cannot issue Canadian settlement accounts, cannot access LVTS/ACH rails directly, and would create additional non-resident counterparty risk for the NVOCC's carrier payment obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is partially available but not unconditionally: OSFI-regulated Canadian banks accept a live interactive video interview for the General Partner's authorized signatories, supplemented by digital identity verification, but Schedule I banks commonly require at least one physical presence or notarized identity verification for partnerships with non-resident limited partners. For the Quebec Limited Partnership (société en commandite), the General Partner's representative should attend an in-branch interview at the bank's corporate centre in Montréal or Toronto, or present a notarized Certificate of Incumbency and a certified copy of the Quebec Registraire des entreprises registration; otherwise account activation is delayed subject to enhanced due diligence. An underwriter may require the physical appearance of any director owning 25% or more of the General Partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: Limited Partnership structure with non-resident limited partners obscures the ultimate natural persons, particularly when capital commitments are funded from offshore jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec evidencing the société en commandite registration; the full executed partnership agreement identifying every Limited Partner holding 25% or more of capital; a notarized beneficial ownership schedule for all partners; 90-day bank statements or asset verification for each capital contributor evidencing source of wealth and source of funds; declarant General Partner resolution; and a completed Standard Corporate KYC form with FINTRAC true-owner attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border EFT activity consistent with freight forwarding creates an ML typology risk: the partnership collects freight payments from clients and disburses to ocean carriers, terminals, and customs brokers, which can be confused with pass-through or money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed NVOCC service contracts and booking confirmations with each principal; original and house Bills of Lading (MB/L and HB/L) referencing cargo, voyage, and container numbers; corresponding ocean carrier invoices and MT103 receipts showing the same reference; voyage-level settlement ledger; payroll and office expense records evidencing real economic substance; and a written AML/CFT policy with transaction monitoring thresholds consistent with PCMLTFA and FINTRAC directives.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control exposure: as a freight forwarder of third-party cargo, the LP may unknowingly forward goods to or from sanctioned entities or controlled destinations, triggering a restricted-party match or a transaction freeze.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented restricted-party screening log covering every shipment and counterparty against OFAC, UN, EU, and Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists; CBP/AES export documentation and customs broker confirmation for U.S.-connected cargo; a written compliance attestation that the General Partner performs dual-use and sanctions screening; sworn beneficial owner declarations as to non-engagement with listed persons; and a bank-requested statutory declaration confirming the NVOCC holds the required regulatory licence and does not provide cover for controlled cargo.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: inbound capital contributions must be received via SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire/CHIPS for USD) using the beneficiary bank's published Standard Settlement Instructions. The remittance field 70 must include the required purpose string: 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - CA_QC_LP - REQ REGISTRATION [number] - ISIC 5229 NVOCC'. No Bank of Canada approval or surrender of foreign currency is required, but each incoming EFT of CAD 10,000 or more must be logged and reportable to FINTRAC; the bank will perform enhanced due diligence and match the remittance narrative against the pre-loaded partnership agreement and source-of-funds dossier. The initial capital should be credited to the Capital Escrow Account, held until the bank's compliance unit releases funds to the Operational Account through an internal journal transfer; verification requires the partner's source-of-funds package, the Quebec partnership certificate, and an executed General Partner capital contribution resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 and MT103 (STP) wires for ocean carrier payments, terminal handling charges, and demurrage/surcharge settlements, with gpi end-to-end tracking; (ii) USD ACH (NACHA) for recurring payments to U.S.-based container lines and warehouse operators; (iii) domestic CAD EFT/PAD via LVTS or ACSS for Canadian rail and trucking sub-contractors; (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit issued or advised under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700/MT707) for high-value charter hire or large prepaid ocean freight where documentary security is required; (v) SWIFT MT202 for cover payments in nostro-cleared USD. Every outgoing instruction must include in field 70 the underlying transport reference (HB/L or MB/L number, voyage, container number) so that the disbursement matches the invoiced freight obligation and avoids FINTRAC 'structuring' indicia.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable vanilla USD/CAD foreign exchange forwards with tenors up to 12 months, available from Schedule I banks without ISDA/MRA restructuring
USD/CAD foreign exchange swaps (simultaneous spot/forward pair) for corridor liquidity management between CAD operational accounts and USD clearing accounts
USD/CAD participating FX options (call/put and zero-cost collars) to protect NVOCC freight tariff margins against adverse USD/CAD movements
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) where the partnership draws a USD-denominated equipment or working-capital loan against CAD cashflows

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible for hedging exposure to non-convertible destination currencies (e.g., restricted LATAM/EEMEA currencies) but are NOT permitted or necessary for USD/CAD, which is a fully deliverable pair; NDF execution requires an ISDA 1992/2002 master agreement with a Canadian authorized derivatives dealer

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual updating declaration for the Quebec limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually during the prescribed annual updating period, generally linked to the anniversary of registration; update changes promptly when required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fees may apply; failure to file annual updating declarations for consecutive years may result in ex officio cancellation of registration and loss of good standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate beneficial owner information confirmation and updating
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirm information through the annual updating declaration; report changes to beneficial ownership or control within the prescribed statutory period, generally 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties may apply for incomplete or inaccurate disclosure; persistent non-compliance may affect registration status and trigger enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due five months after the partnership fiscal period-end when the partnership satisfies federal filing criteria
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties may apply, including penalties based on the number of partners and days outstanding; repeated non-compliance may trigger CRA review and partner reassessments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Information Return, Form TP-600
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due five months after the partnership fiscal period-end where Quebec filing conditions are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest may apply; failure to provide partnership information may impair partner tax reporting and trigger audit activity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec enterprise information updates for legal address, partners, business activities, and authorized representatives
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within the statutory update period after a change and reflect the information in the next annual updating declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties may apply for late or inaccurate information; material omissions may result in notices, compliance action, or cancellation of registration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general Quebec statutory independent-audit requirement applies solely because the entity is a limited partnership. An audit may be required by the partnership agreement, financing documents, limited partner agreement, investor requirements, regulated activities, or applicable federal or Quebec tax reporting conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises are generally applicable for private partnership financial statements; IFRS may be used where elected or contractually required. Tax returns must follow CRA and Revenu Quebec tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain current records of limited partners, general partners, partnership interests, transfers, voting or control rights, and ultimate beneficial owners. Confirm the information in the annual updating declaration and report changes within the applicable statutory deadline. Each transfer of a partnership interest must be documented in the partnership register and tested for changes in beneficial ownership or control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners and partnership interests
Register of partnership-interest transfers and contributions
Register of ultimate beneficial owners and control information
Executed limited partnership agreement and amendments
Minute book or written resolutions of partners and management committee, where applicable
Accounting records, financial statements, tax filings, and supporting documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 500-1,500 per year for Quebec registered-office, correspondence, filing, and partnership-administration services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000-15,000 for a basic independent audit; no audit fee is mandatory where no audit obligation applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the Quebec Limited Partnership ('LP') level: the LP is fiscally transparent and is not a corporation. Partners are taxed on allocated income; an individual partner's top combined federal–Quebec marginal rate is approximately 53.31%, and a corporate partner's combined general rate is 26.5% (federal general corporate rate 15% + Quebec general rate 11.5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday applies to ocean freight forwarding/NVOCC services. Freight-forwarding income allocated to a Canadian corporate partner can benefit from the federal small business deduction (9% federal plus reduced Quebec rate) only if the underlying active business is carried on through a Canadian-controlled private corporation, not directly by the LP. No preferential NVOCC tax deduction exists under Quebec law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CRA Form T5013 (Partnership Information Return) and T5013 slips, filed electronically through CRA's 'My Business Account', 'Represent a Client', or approved E-filer software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; partners also remit partnership income taxes quarterly in instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a calendar-year LP, CRA requires the T5013 return and the T5013 Summary to be filed no later than March 31 of the following calendar year, and T5013 slips must be provided to partners by the last day of February.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the LP's aggregate NVOCC ocean freight forwarding revenue less directly related vessel, container, haulage, and booking costs; this income is allocated under the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners' shares are included in the T5013 allocation; the LP must identify each non-resident partner's residence and postal code in the T5013 'province/territory of residence' field using country code rather than a Quebec postal code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 30 — Limited partner's share of loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records loss allocated to limited partners; a limited partner may deduct only losses up to the 'at-risk amount' (contributed capital plus unpaid committed capital/loans). Excess losses are suspended.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Restrict the loss to the non-resident limited partner's Canadian tax basis and at-risk amount; suspended losses are tracked in CRA Form T5013 schedules and cannot be used to create or increase a negative adjusted cost base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List each partner's name, business number, percentage interest, class (general versus limited partner), country of residence, and share of income/loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident limited partners, attach the DTA residence jurisdiction and confirm whether any Part XIII withholding was applied; enter 'N/A' in SIN field and provide foreign tax identification number.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CRA late-filing penalty: CAD 25 per partner per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500, plus additional penalty for repeated gross negligence; unreasonable failure to file can lead to summary conviction under the Income Tax Act. Revenu Quebec applies separate daily penalties for late RL-15 filings and can charge interest on unreported Quebec tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Revenu Quebec RL-15 (Releve de revenus de societe de personnes) and partnership financial statements, filed via Revenu Quebec's 'Transmission electronique' / Mon dossier d'entreprise portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the LP's fiscal period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The RL-15 filing copy is due with Revenu Quebec no later than the last day of February following the calendar year in which the partnership fiscal period ends; partner copies must be issued by the same date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), legal name, address, and Canada Revenue Agency business number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the LP's Quebec permanent establishment; NVOCC activity conducted through a Canadian office in Quebec creates a substantive provincial presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec-source active business income or loss from freight forwarding, allocated to each partner on the same percentages used at the federal level.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty provisions in the allocation; Quebec taxes the non-resident partner's share only if the partnership has a Quebec permanent establishment or the partner is carrying on business in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C — Provincial deductions and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim only Quebec-specific deductions and refundable credits attributed to the partnership, such as the Quebec tax credit for transportation/logistics investment, if coded to the LP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident limited partner is generally ineligible for refundable Quebec tax credits unless the income is taxable in Quebec and the partner files a Quebec income tax return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Quebec can impose a minimum penalty of CAD 100 and a maximum of CAD 2,500 for late/false RL-15 information returns, plus daily late-filing penalties and interest; deliberate omissions are prosecuted as tax evasion under the Tax Administration Act with fines up to 200% of the evaded provincial tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act for dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident. The LP itself does not pay dividends; distributions to non-resident partners are partnership distributions. A non-resident partner's share of Canadian-source partnership business income is generally subject to Part I tax on a net basis if the partnership carries on business in Canada, and to Part XIII withholding at 25% on amounts that are paid or credited to the non-resident partner as income allocations where no Part I election applies. Return of contributed capital is not subject to withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident partner must provide the LP with a valid certificate of tax residence (TRC) and, for reduced withholding, Form NR301 (Application for Treaty-Based Waiver of Withholding Tax) before the distribution date. The LP/withholding agent must keep the TRC, Form NR301, and the treaty interpretation memorandum on file and transmit the information to CRA on request. If tax was over-withheld, the non-resident partner must file Form NR302/NR303 with CRA within two years of the withholding date to claim a refund. For Quebec, attach the TRC to the Quebec return and claim the corresponding provincial treaty reduction via the Revenu Quebec portal. A single set of DTA residence evidence accepted by CRA is generally sufficient for Quebec purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate: 25% for both interest and royalties paid by a Canadian resident to a non-resident. Treaty rates are generally lower: most Canadian DTAs reduce interest to 0-15% (Canada-US arm's length interest commonly 0%); patent/industrial royalties are commonly 10% under Canadian DTAs, with 0% reserved for certain literary, dramatic, musical and artistic copyright royalties under the Canada-US treaty and similar DTA provisions. For NVOCC operations, payments to foreign carriers, container lessors, logistics software licensors, and group financing entities must be scrutinized for hidden royalty characterization.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million in aggregate value of specified non-arm's length transactions with each non-resident in the year triggers mandatory CRA Form T106 (Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents). Contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (OECD master file/local file) must be prepared for any controlled transaction and is required, at a minimum, for large groups with consolidated revenue meeting the country-by-country reporting threshold of EUR 750 million or its Canadian-dollar equivalent as adjusted by CRA; the CRA can require documentation for lower-threshold transactions if non-arm's length pricing risk is identified.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone 'Economic Substance Regulations' code, but the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR, paragraph 245(2) ITA), the foreign accrual property income rules, and the 'central mind and management' / permanent establishment tests impose a de facto substance requirement. An LP claiming treaty benefits or charging intercompany fees to a related offshore booking company must show real operational substance in Quebec: physical office, employees responsible for freight sales and operations, contractual risk assumption, and commercial decision-making. Quebec's Registraire des entreprises also requires a real registered office and discloses partners/directors; a passive 'mailbox' LP with no staff is treated as a shell and attracts CRA recharacterization, GAAR penalties and possible denial of DTA benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / false reporting (federal and Quebec)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating NVOCC gross revenue, inflating container, port, or haulage costs, fabricating invoices from a related offshore company, or destroying freight-forwarding records after receiving a CRA audit request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross negligence penalty equal to 50% of the understated federal tax; Quebec civil penalty up to 50% of the evaded provincial tax; criminal prosecution under subsection 239(1) of the Income Tax Act and Quebec Tax Administration Act carrying fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Partners and directors who authorized false filings are jointly and severally liable; corporate veil does not protect a general partner; travel bans, freezing orders, and orders of civil restitution can be issued, and convicted individuals may receive imprisonment, director disqualification, and seizure of personal Canadian assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Quebec LP as a bare intermediary that books NVOCC income in Canada while all operational risk, management, and cash-flow decisions are taken in a no-tax jurisdiction, with no economic substance and with the only purpose of eliminating Canadian tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA reassessment disregarding the LP for tax purposes, applying the GAAR, reallocating income to the beneficial owner, denying treaty relief, and imposing GAAR penalties (introduced for transactions after 2023 with an additional punitive amount) plus interest; a misused LP can also be struck from the Quebec registry for non-respect of the Companies Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner ('commandite') has unlimited liability; limited partners who engage in management or who misuse the LP as a sham can be personally liable. Relevant persons can be pursued for civil restitution, penal travel bans, and prohibition orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's length freight-forwarding, management, or charter fees to a non-resident affiliate in a manner that departs from arm's length value, or failing to file Form T106 within the return due date despite crossing the CAD 1 million transaction threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA adjusts taxable income under section 247 ITA and applies a transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the net adjustment, plus interest; failure to file T106 can incur a separate penalty of CAD 100 per day up to CAD 2,500 for each failure; Canada also applies treaty-related secondary adjustments in eligible cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be liable for the LP's unremitted withholding and for unpaid taxes if they signed or directed false transfer-pricing documents; CRA can assess director liability under section 227.1 and impose contempt orders for non-compliance with document production orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Part XIII withholding failure on non-resident partners / cross-border payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing Canadian-source income allocations to non-resident limited partners, or paying royalties/interest to non-resident related parties, without withholding the required 25% Part XIII tax and without a valid Form NR301/TRC on file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The LP is liable for the full amount of unwithheld Part XIII tax, plus penalties under section 227(9) of 10% plus interest; CRA can assess the tax even if the non-resident recipient has failed to file a Canadian return; refund of excess withholding is only available to the non-resident, not to the LP.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are jointly and severally liable for unremitted withholding taxes; CRA may issue named assessments, garnishment on Canadian bank accounts, and the Cour du Quebec can impose travel bans and imprisonment for wilful non-remittance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / unlicensed NVOCC / financial intermediary misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as an NVOCC or ocean freight consolidator without a valid service/agency contract, issuing house bills of lading without a registered business in Quebec, or accepting large cash or third-party wire freight payments without FINTRAC reporting and a written AML compliance program.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fines under the Canada Shipping Act and provincial consumer protection laws; FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for individuals and CAD 2,000,000 for entities; QST/GST registration and common carrier duties apply; enhanced audit scrutiny by CRA and Revenu Quebec.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals responsible for laundering proceeds via freight payment rails face Criminal Code fraud/laundering charges punishable by imprisonment up to 14 years; directors can be subject to asset forfeiture, personal fines, and travel restrictions pending extradition/prosecution.
